items.title: feat: hermes plugins install/remove/list CLI command
items.body:
## Problem

Hermes v0.3.0 ships a plugin architecture (`~/.hermes/plugins/`) but has no CLI command to install or manage plugins. Users must manually clone repos into the plugins directory. There's no discoverability, no post-install guidance, no update mechanism, and no removal command.

## Proposed Solution

Add a `hermes plugins` subcommand:

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `hermes plugins install <git-url\|owner/repo>` | Clone a plugin into `~/.hermes/plugins/` |
| `hermes plugins install --force <identifier>` | Remove existing and reinstall |
| `hermes plugins update <name>` | Pull latest changes for an installed plugin |
| `hermes plugins remove <name>` | Remove an installed plugin |
| `hermes plugins list` | Rich-formatted table of installed plugins |

### Key features

- **Manifest-based naming** — install directory uses the `name` field from `plugin.yaml`, not the repo name. e.g. `hermes plugins install anpicasso/hermes-plugin-chrome-profiles` installs to `~/.hermes/plugins/chrome-profiles/` because the manifest says `name: chrome-profiles`. Falls back to repo name if no manifest.
- **Manifest version checking** — plugins may declare `manifest_version: 1` in `plugin.yaml`. The installer checks compatibility and fails with a clear message if the plugin requires a newer version.
- **Fail fast on conflict** — if the target directory already exists, install fails immediately with guidance to use `--force` or `hermes plugins update`.
- **`--force` reinstall** — `hermes plugins install --force <identifier>` removes the existing plugin directory and installs fresh.
- **`update` command** — `hermes plugins update <name>` runs `git pull --ff-only` on the plugin directory. Fails if the plugin wasn't installed from git.
- **`.example` file bootstrapping** — after cloning, any `*.example` files are copied to their real names (e.g. `config.yaml.example` → `config.yaml`). Skips if the real file already exists so reinstalls don't nuke user config.
- **`after-install.md`** — if a plugin ships this file, render it with Rich Markdown post-install (config location, usage instructions). Falls back to a default confirmation message.
- **Gateway restart hint** — after install, prints a reminder to restart the gateway for the plugin to take effect.
- **owner/repo shorthand** — resolves to GitHub automatically
- **Shallow clone** — uses `--depth 1` for minimal disk usage
- **Aliases** — `remove`/`rm`/`uninstall`, `list`/`ls`

### Example plugins

| Plugin | Description | Status |
|--------|-------------|--------|
| [hermes-plugin-chrome-profiles](https://github.com/anpicasso/hermes-plugin-chrome-profiles) | Browser profile switching via CDP — local launch + remote profiles | ✅ Stable |
| [hermes-plugin-acp-client](https://github.com/anpicasso/hermes-plugin-acp-client) | ACP client for OpenCode agents via stdio/NDJSON — discovers configured agents/modes automatically | 🚧 WIP |

```bash
hermes plugins install anpicasso/hermes-plugin-chrome-profiles
hermes plugins install anpicasso/hermes-plugin-acp-client
```

items.title: [Bug]: Newline/multiline input broken in Ghostty terminal on macOS
items.body:
## Description

Pressing Shift+Enter (or any expected newline key combo) in the Hermes TUI does not insert a newline — instead it sends raw escape sequences (e.g. `[13;2u`) directly into the input buffer.

## Environment

- **Terminal:** Ghostty (macOS)
- **OS:** macOS (Apple Silicon M1)
- **Hermes version:** v0.3.0

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch `hermes` TUI in Ghostty on macOS
2. Press Shift+Enter to attempt a multiline message
3. Instead of a newline, escape sequence characters appear in the input (e.g. `[13;2u[13;2u`)

## Expected Behavior

Shift+Enter (or a documented key combo) inserts a newline in the input field, allowing multiline messages before sending.

## Actual Behavior

Raw escape sequences are injected into the input instead of a newline character. The message cannot be composed across multiple lines.

## Notes

Ghostty uses the [Kitty keyboard protocol](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/keyboard-protocol/) which encodes modifier keys differently than traditional terminals. The TUI input handler may need to handle `CSI 13;2u` (Shift+Enter in Kitty protocol) as a newline.

items.title: delegate_task fails: _saved_tool_names not in scope after _build_child_agent/_run_single_child split
items.body:
## Bug: `delegate_task` fails with `NameError: name '_saved_tool_names' is not defined`

### Version
v0.3.0 (commit from 2026-03-17)

### Provider
Anthropic (Claude Max OAuth), also confirmed with gateway-initiated sessions

### Description

Every `delegate_task` call fails during subagent execution. The `_run_single_child()` function references a local variable `_saved_tool_names` that is defined in a different function (`_build_child_agent()`), causing a `NameError` in the `finally` block.

### Error

```
Error executing tool: Error during OpenAI-compatible API call #2: name '_saved_tool_names' is not defined
```

### Root Cause

In `tools/delegate_tool.py`, the v0.3.0 refactor split child agent construction and execution into two separate functions:

1. **`_build_child_agent()`** (line 150) — saves the parent's tool names at line 178:
   ```python
   _saved_tool_names = list(model_tools._last_resolved_tool_names)
   ```

2. **`_run_single_child()`** (line 250) — attempts to restore them at line 375:
   ```python
   finally:
       model_tools._last_resolved_tool_names = _saved_tool_names
   ```

`_saved_tool_names` is a local variable in `_build_child_agent()`. It is never passed to `_run_single_child()` as a parameter, and there is no shared scope between the two functions. The `finally` block at line 375 always raises `NameError`.

### Why Tests Don't Catch It

The existing test suite in `tests/tools/test_delegate.py` mocks `_run_single_child` in most integration tests (lines 126, 140, 158, 170, 187, 773), so the real `finally` block never executes. The interrupt tests (`test_interactive_interrupt.py`, `test_cli_interrupt_subagent.py`, `test_real_interrupt_subagent.py`) call `_run_single_child` directly but don't set up `_saved_tool_names` in the calling scope, which either gets masked by other mock patching or raises the same error that gets caught elsewhere.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Start a Hermes session (CLI or gateway)
2. Trigger any `delegate_task` call — single or batch
3. Subagent construction succeeds (`_build_child_agent` returns)
4. `_run_single_child` runs the subagent
5. On completion (or error), the `finally` block at line 375 raises `NameError`

This is 100% reproducible — not intermittent.

### Suggested Fix

Pass `_saved_tool_names` through to `_run_single_child`, or move the save/restore logic entirely into `_run_single_child`:

**Option A — Pass as parameter:**
```python
def _build_child_agent(...):
    _saved_tool_names = list(model_tools._last_resolved_tool_names)
    # ... build child ...
    child._saved_parent_tool_names = _saved_tool_names  # stash on child object
    return child

def _run_single_child(...):
    _saved_tool_names = getattr(child, '_saved_parent_tool_names', [])
    try:
        ...
    finally:
        model_tools._last_resolved_tool_names = _saved_tool_names
```

**Option B — Save/restore in `_run_single_child`:**
```python
def _run_single_child(task_index, goal, child=None, parent_agent=None, **_kwargs):
    _saved_tool_names = list(model_tools._last_resolved_tool_names)
    try:
        ...
    finally:
        model_tools._last_resolved_tool_names = _saved_tool_names
```

Option B is simpler and keeps the save/restore in the same scope. The save in `_build_child_agent()` (line 178) can then be removed.

### Impact

Delegation is completely broken in v0.3.0. All `delegate_task` calls fail. This affects both CLI and gateway sessions.

items.title: MEDIA: tag fails to send files - document upload not working
items.body:
## Bug Description
The `MEDIA:` tag for sending files via Telegram is broken. When including `MEDIA:/path/to/file` in a response, the file path is sent as plain text instead of the actual file being uploaded.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Create a file: `echo "test content" > /tmp/test.txt`
2. Ask the agent to send it: "Send me this file: MEDIA:/tmp/test.txt"
3. The bot responds with the literal text "MEDIA:/tmp/test.txt" instead of uploading the file

## Expected Behavior
The file should be uploaded as a document attachment via the Telegram Bot API.

## Actual Behavior
The file path is sent as plain text message.

## Root Cause Analysis

### Issue 1: Base Class Default Behavior
In `base.py` line 562, `send_document()` defaults to:
```python
def send_document(self, file_path: str, caption: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
    return self.send_message(file_path)  # Just sends path as text!
```

### Issue 2: Adapter Override Not Being Called
`TelegramAdapter.send_document()` exists (lines 282-294) but is **not being invoked** when processing `MEDIA:` tags. The gateway's message processing chain is not correctly routing to the adapter's method.

### Issue 3: Regex Pattern Issues
The regex in `platforms/messaging.py` line 268 has issues with spaces in filenames:
```python
MEDIA_PATTERN = re.compile(r'MEDIA:\s*(\S+)', re.IGNORECASE)
```
The `\S+` stops at first space, breaking paths like `/path/to/my file.txt`.

## Suggested Fix

1. **Trace the call chain** in `handle_message()` to ensure `TelegramAdapter.send_document()` is invoked
2. **Fix the regex** to handle spaces:
   ```python
   MEDIA_PATTERN = re.compile(r'MEDIA:\s*(.+?)(?=\s+(?:MEDIA:|$|\n)|$)', re.IGNORECASE)
   ```
3. **Add logging** to verify the adapter method is reached

## Environment
- Hermes Gateway version: latest
- Platform: Telegram
- Python version: 3.11+

## Additional Context
I worked around this by using `python-telegram-bot` directly to call `send_document()`, which confirms the Telegram Bot API works fine - it's the gateway's internal routing that's broken.

items.title: Bug: OpenClaw CLI provider passes large web content as CLI argument (PR #165)
items.body:
## Bug Description

In PR #165 (Add OpenClaw CLI provider support), the implementation passes the **entire web page content as a CLI argument** via `--message <prompt>`.

## Location

The bug is in `src/llm/cli.ts`:

```typescript
const args = [
  "agent",
  "--agent",
  model && model.trim().length > 0 ? model.trim() : "main",
  "--message",
  prompt,   // ← BUG: Entire web page content passed here!
  "--json",
  "--timeout",
  String(Math.max(1, Math.ceil(timeoutMs / 1000))),
];
```

## Why It's a Problem

1. **Shell argument limits**: Most systems cap CLI arguments at 128KB-2MB. Web pages can be 50KB-500KB+, which will cause failures
2. **No stdin support**: The implementation should pass content via stdin (like other CLI tools do) instead of CLI arguments
3. **Test was flawed**: The PR author's smoke test used a tiny message:
   ```bash
   printf 'OpenClaw summarizes through the main agent.\n' | ...
   ```
   This works, but real usage with full web pages will break

## Suggested Fix

Use stdin or file input instead of CLI arguments:

**Option 1: Use stdin (recommended)**
```typescript
const args = ["agent", "--agent", model, "-", "--json", "--timeout", ...];
// Then pass prompt via stdin in execCliWithInput
```

**Option 2: Write to temp file**
```typescript
// Write prompt to temp file, then use --message-file (if supported)
```

## Test Case

To reproduce:
1. Summarize a large web page (>100KB of content)
2. Observe failure due to argument size limits

## Additional Notes

- This is a great feature addition (OpenClaw support)!
- The implementation is otherwise solid — this is just an input method issue
- Works fine for small content, but needs fixing for production use with real web pages

items.title: [UX] Rate limit errors (429) should show user-friendly message with configurable retry instead of traceback
items.body:
## Problem

When hitting API rate limits (HTTP 429), Hermes currently displays a full traceback error to the user. This is a poor UX for a transient condition that the system should handle gracefully.

## Current Behavior

```
ERROR:anthropic:Rate limit exceeded (429)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/hermes/path/to/file.py", line 123, in function_name
    response = await client.chat(...)
anthropic.RateLimitError: Rate limit exceeded
```

## Desired Behavior

1. **User-friendly message**: Display a clear, concise message like:
   - "Rate limit reached. Waiting 30s before retry..." (with countdown)
   - "Rate limit active. Retry in 15s."
   - Or similar clean messaging

2. **Configurable automatic retry**: Add config option(s) for rate limit handling:
   - `retry.on_rate_limit: true` (default)
   - `retry.max_rate_limit_retries: 5` (default)
   - `retry.rate_limit_backoff_base: 30` (seconds, default - exponential backoff)
   - `retry.rate_limit_wait_max: 300` (max seconds to wait)

3. **Show progress**: Display countdown or progress indicator during wait:
   - CLI: "Rate limit hit. Waiting 30s... [████░░░░░░] 12/30"
   - Gateway platforms: "Rate limit hit. Retrying in 30s..." (update as countdown progresses)

4. **Graceful failure**: If retries exhausted or disabled, show clean error:
   - "Rate limit persisted after 5 retries. Please try again later."
   - No traceback for transient errors

## Additional Notes

- This applies to all providers, not just Anthropic
- Current code already has some 429 retry logic (see PR #1585), but user-facing messaging still shows traces
- Should respect provider-specific Retry-After headers when available

## Priority

Medium - UX improvement, system already attempts retries internally

items.title: [Bug]: gateway --replace can miss existing script-style gateway processes, allowing duplicate instances and duplicate Discord replies
items.body:
### Bug Description

Restarting the gateway with `hermes gateway run --replace` can fail to detect an already-running gateway when the live process was started via the script-style command path:

- `/.../hermes_cli/main.py gateway run --replace`

When that happens, a second gateway process starts instead of replacing the first one. In Discord, both gateway processes consume the same incoming messages, which can produce duplicate replies (especially noticeable in active threads/channels).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start Hermes gateway using a script-style invocation that yields a live cmdline like:
   - `/path/to/venv/bin/python /path/to/hermes_cli/main.py gateway run --replace`
2. Restart the gateway again with:
   - `hermes gateway run --replace`
3. Observe that the existing process is not always recognized/replaced.
4. Send a Discord message in a server/channel handled by the gateway.
5. Observe duplicate replies because multiple gateway processes are active.

### Expected Behavior

`--replace` should reliably detect and replace any existing Hermes gateway instance, regardless of whether it was started via:

- `python -m hermes_cli.main gateway ...`
- `hermes gateway ...`
- `/path/to/hermes_cli/main.py gateway ...`

Only one gateway process should remain running.

### Actual Behavior

Process detection logic misses script-style command lines containing:

- `hermes_cli/main.py gateway`

This allows duplicate gateway processes to remain active, which can lead to duplicate Discord responses because both instances receive the same events.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Discord

### Operating System

Linux

### Python Version

3.11

### Hermes Version

Current `main` checkout as of 2026-03-17 (local repro in `~/.hermes/hermes-agent`)

### Relevant Logs / Traceback

Symptoms included:

- two concurrent gateway processes with cmdlines matching `hermes_cli/main.py gateway run --replace`
- duplicate Discord replies
- Discord auto-thread warnings such as:
  - `Auto-thread creation failed: 400 Bad Request (error code: 160004): A thread has already been created for this message`

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The gateway duplicate-instance guard and helper process scan recognize these patterns:

- `hermes_cli.main gateway`
- `hermes gateway`
- `gateway/run.py`

But they do not recognize the script-style invocation form:

- `hermes_cli/main.py gateway`

Relevant areas:

- `gateway/status.py`
  - `_looks_like_gateway_process()`
  - `_record_looks_like_gateway()`
- `hermes_cli/gateway.py`
  - `find_gateway_pids()`

As a result, `get_running_pid()` / replacement logic can fail to identify the existing gateway, so `--replace` does not actually replace it.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Include `hermes_cli/main.py gateway` in the recognized gateway command-line patterns anywhere process identity is checked.

I locally validated that adding this pattern fixes detection and prevents duplicate live gateway processes. I also added a regression test for script-style cmdline detection in `tests/gateway/test_status.py`.

items.title: fix(banner): honcho/homeassistant tools show as disabled (red) at startup
items.body:
## Bug

The startup banner shows honcho and homeassistant tools in red (disabled color) even when they are properly configured and functional.

## Root cause

The banner renders at the start of `cli.py:run()` (line 5641), but the agent is initialized lazily on first message (`_init_agent` at line 5197). Honcho tools use a `check_fn` (`_check_honcho_available`) that requires `set_session_context()` to have been called, which only happens inside `_activate_honcho()` during agent init.

Timeline:
1. `run()` starts -> `show_banner()` called
2. Banner calls `check_tool_availability()` -> `_check_honcho_available()` returns `False` (no session context yet)
3. Honcho tools rendered in red
4. User sends first message -> `_init_agent()` -> `_activate_honcho()` -> `set_session_context()`
5. Tools are now actually available, but banner already rendered

## Impact

Cosmetic only. The tools work correctly once the first message is sent. But it's confusing -- users see red tools and may think honcho is broken.

## Suggested fix

In `banner.py`, don't mark tools as disabled if their toolset has a `check_fn`. These are runtime-gated (activate lazily), not misconfigured. Show them in normal color or a distinct "pending" color instead of error red.

Affected toolsets: `honcho`, `homeassistant_tools`, `send_message` (any toolset with a `check_fn`).

items.title: Race condition in concurrent tool batching for overlapping file mutations
items.body:
## Summary
`AIAgent._execute_tool_calls()` currently decides between sequential and concurrent execution at the batch level, but the concurrency gate is too coarse for write-capable tools.

When a model emits multiple tool calls in one turn, overlapping file mutations such as `write_file(path="src/a.py")` + `patch(path="src/a.py")` can race each other if they enter the concurrent path. That can produce nondeterministic file state, stale patch application, and hard-to-reproduce failures.

## Why this matters
- Some multi-tool batches are genuinely independent and should stay parallel for latency.
- Some batches target the same file or subtree and must stay ordered.
- The current gating logic does not distinguish those cases precisely enough.

## Repro shape
1. Emit multiple tool calls in one assistant turn.
2. Include overlapping file mutations against the same path.
3. Allow the batch onto the concurrent execution path.
4. Observe nondeterministic ordering / final file contents depending on thread timing.

## Expected behavior
Concurrent batching should allow independent tool calls, but overlapping file mutations should be forced back to sequential execution.

A reasonable fix is to make the batching gate path-aware for file tools, so disjoint targets can still run concurrently while overlapping targets cannot.

items.title: [Bug] Gateway approval system intercepts unrelated user responses (yes to clarify question approves pending dangerous command)
items.body:
## Bug Description

When the gateway has a pending dangerous command approval and the agent subsequently asks a clarifying question (via the `clarify` tool), the user's response to the clarify question can be incorrectly intercepted as an approval for the dangerous command.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Agent attempts a command that triggers the dangerous command approval system
2. Approval system stores pending approval in `self._pending_approvals[session_key]`
3. Agent asks an unrelated clarifying question (e.g., "Do you want me to save this as a skill?")
4. User responds "yes" to answer the clarifying question
5. **Bug:** Gateway intercepts "yes", pops the pending approval, and executes the dangerous command
6. User's clarify response is consumed as command approval instead of being passed to the agent

## Expected Behavior

The "yes" response should be passed to the agent as an answer to the clarifying question, not intercepted as command approval.

## Actual Behavior

The approval check in `gateway/run.py` lines 1500-1525 intercepts the message before context awareness:

```python
# Lines 1502-1504
if session_key_preview in self._pending_approvals:
    user_text = event.text.strip().lower()
    if user_text in ("yes", "y", "approve", "ok", "go", "do it"):
        # ... executes the pending dangerous command
```

There is no awareness of whether the user was responding to:
1. A pending command approval (intended)
2. A clarify tool question (bug)
3. General conversation (bug)

## Impact

**Security concern:** User says "yes" to "Do you want me to save this as a skill?" and the system interprets it as "yes, execute that dangerous command"

## Suggested Fix Options

**Option A: Timeout-based expiry**
- Add timestamp to pending approvals
- Expire them after ~60s
- Reduces window but does not eliminate the race

**Option B: Context awareness**
- Track when clarify tool is awaiting response
- Do not intercept messages if agent is mid-turn waiting for clarify response

**Option C: Explicit approval syntax**
- Require `/approve` or `!yes` instead of bare "yes"
- Safest but worse UX

**Option D: Sequential ordering (recommended)**
- Track the message ID that triggered the approval request
- Only accept approval responses if no other agent output (like clarify questions) has been sent since the approval prompt

## Environment

- Hermes gateway (Discord/Telegram/Slack adapters)
- File: `gateway/run.py` lines 1500-1525

## Related

Upstream Claude Code has similar but different issues:
- anthropics/claude-code#31858 - `yes` executes as Unix command (different root cause)

items.body:
## Feature Request: Multiple Provider Presets in YAML Config

### Current Behavior
Currently, switching between different providers requires destructive edits to the YAML config - changing the base URL and default model name each time. This is tedious and error-prone when working with multiple providers frequently.

### Desired Behavior
I would like to be able to configure any number of providers as presets in the YAML config file, then switch between them non-destructively (similar to how the new `/model` command works for model switching).

Example config structure:
```yaml
providers:
  anthropic:
    type: anthropic
    model: claude-sonnet-4-20250514
    api_key: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}
    
  openrouter:
    type: openrouter
    model: anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet
    base_url: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
    api_key: ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}
    
  local:
    type: openai-compatible
    model: meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct
    base_url: http://localhost:8000/v1
    api_key: dummy

default_provider: anthropic
```

Then a command like `/provider` or similar to switch between presets:
```
/provider openrouter
# or integrate this into /model command
```

### Benefits
- Non-destructive switching between providers
- Keep all provider configurations in one place
- Easy A/B testing between providers
- Maintain separate API keys, base URLs, and models per provider
- Better ergonomics for users who work with multiple providers regularly

### Alternative Considerations
Could this be integrated into the existing `/model` command's provider auto-detection, or would a separate `/provider` command be clearer?

Thanks for considering this enhancement - Hermes Agent is fantastic!

### Bug Description

The browser tool claims to support connecting to a user-supplied Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint via the `BROWSER_CDP_URL` environment variable, but the connection fails even when the CDP endpoint is confirmed working via HTTP.

The error message indicates the tool is not using the full websocket URL from `BROWSER_CDP_URL` — it shows `ws://localhost:9222` instead of the complete `ws://localhost:9222/devtools/browser/<uuid>` that was set.

- Tested with Chromium (not Chrome) on Wayland/Ozone platform.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start Chromium with remote debugging enabled:
   ```bash
   chromium --remote-debugging-port=9222

items.title: [Bug]: Cron jobs to WhatsApp fail with Baileys jidDecode error when deliver uses human-readable contact label
items.body:
### Bug Description

 **Summary**

  When scheduling Hermes cron jobs that auto-deliver results to WhatsApp, jobs execute successfully but delivery fails if the deliver field is set using the human-readable label shown by
  send_message(action="list") (e.g. whatsapp:Alice (dm)). The cron scheduler treats the portion after whatsapp: as a literal WhatsApp JID and passes it to the WhatsApp bridge, which then
  fails with a Baileys jidDecode error. Manual WhatsApp conversations and gateway-driven messages work fine; the issue is specific to cron auto-delivery.

 
  **Environment**

  • OS: Linux (modern 6.x kernel)
  • Hermes Agent: current main (as of mid‑March 2026)
  • Node: 18.x
  • Python: 3.12.x
  • WhatsApp bridge: scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.js (Baileys-based)


  **What works**

  • Gateway WhatsApp integration is healthy:
    • Manual conversations between the agent and a WhatsApp contact work.
    • ~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log shows lines like:


      2026-03-18 08:15:00,708 INFO gateway.platforms.base: [Whatsapp] Sending response (626 chars) to 12345678901234@lid
      2026-03-18 11:44:09,279 INFO gateway.platforms.base: [Whatsapp] Sending response (682 chars) to 12345678901234@lid
      2026-03-18 13:22:07,525 INFO gateway.platforms.base: [Whatsapp] Sending response (147 chars) to 12345678901234@lid

  • ~/.hermes/channel_directory.json correctly maps the WhatsApp contact:


```
      {
        "platforms": {
          "whatsapp": [
            {
              "id": "12345678901234@lid",
              "name": "Alice",
              "type": "dm",
              "thread_id": null
            }
          ]
        }
      }
```



  **`What fails`**

  When a cron job is configured with deliver using the label shown in the channel directory or send_message(action="list"), e.g.:

 ```
 {
    "id": "315e6f2a8f57",
    "name": "whatsapp-cron-example",
    "deliver": "whatsapp:Alice (dm)",
    "origin": {
      "platform": "whatsapp",
      "chat_id": "12345678901234@lid",
      "chat_name": "Alice",
      "thread_id": null
    },
    ...
  }
```

  the cron job executes and output is written to ~/.hermes/cron/output/<job_id>/...md, but delivery to WhatsApp fails with errors like:

  2026-03-18 14:00:33,347 ERROR cron.scheduler: Job '315e6f2a8f57': delivery error: WhatsApp bridge error (500): {"error":"Cannot destructure property 'user' of 'jidDecode(...)' as it is
  undefined."}

  A similar earlier run showed:

  2026-03-18 13:24:35,109 ERROR cron.scheduler: Job '9cc2b836678f': delivery error: WhatsApp bridge error (500): {"error":"Cannot destructure property 'user' of 'jidDecode(...)' as it is
  undefined."}

  The cron scheduler reports the job as executed and last_status: "ok", but the WhatsApp device never receives the cron result.


### Steps to Reproduce


  1. Run gateway + WhatsApp bridge and pair successfully, so that:
    • Manual chats with a contact (e.g. “Alice”) work.
    • channel_directory.json contains an entry similar to:


```
       {
         "id": "12345678901234@lid",
         "name": "Alice",
         "type": "dm"
       }

```
  2. Create a cron job from that WhatsApp conversation, with e.g.:
    • origin.platform = "whatsapp"
    • origin.chat_id = "12345678901234@lid"
    • deliver = "whatsapp:Alice (dm)"

       (i.e. use the human-readable label that appears in the “Available messaging targets” list, including the  (dm) suffix).
  3. Let the job run at its scheduled time, or trigger it manually (e.g. via cron.jobs.trigger_job or hermes cron run <job_id>).
  4. Observe:
    • A new output file is created under ~/.hermes/cron/output/<job_id>/...md (job ran successfully).
    • ~/.hermes/logs/errors.log or gateway.log contains:


       ERROR cron.scheduler: Job '<job_id>': delivery error: WhatsApp bridge error (500): {"error":"Cannot destructure property 'user' of 'jidDecode(...)' as it is undefined."}

    • No message is delivered to WhatsApp for that cron run.
  5. Now edit the same job in ~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json to instead use a valid JID:
    • Either deliver: "origin"
    • Or deliver: "whatsapp:12345678901234@lid"
  6. Trigger the job again and observe that delivery now succeeds and the cron result appears in the WhatsApp chat.

### Expected Behavior


  • Cron jobs should be able to use the same human-friendly deliver target format that the documentation and send_message(action="list") present to the user, e.g.:
    • deliver: "whatsapp:Alice (dm)"
  • In that case, the cron scheduler should:
    1. Parse platform_name = "whatsapp", target_ref = "Alice (dm)".
    2. Strip display-only suffixes like " (dm)".
    3. Use gateway.channel_directory.resolve_channel_name("whatsapp", "Alice") to resolve to the underlying JID 12345678901234@lid.
    4. Pass the resolved JID to _send_to_platform() / the WhatsApp bridge.
  • No Baileys jidDecode errors, and the message appears on the WhatsApp device.

### Actual Behavior


  • cron/scheduler.py::_resolve_delivery_target() currently does:


```
    if ":" in deliver:
        platform_name, chat_id = deliver.split(":", 1)
        return {
            "platform": platform_name,
            "chat_id": chat_id,
            "thread_id": None,
        }

```
  • For deliver = "whatsapp:Alice (dm)", this yields:
    • platform_name = "whatsapp"
    • chat_id = "Alice (dm)"
  • This literal string is passed to:


    from tools.send_message_tool import _send_to_platform
    ...
    result = asyncio.run(_send_to_platform(platform, pconfig, chat_id, content, thread_id=thread_id))

  • _send_to_platform() then calls _send_whatsapp(extra, chat_id, message), which POSTs:

```

    { "chatId": "Alice (dm)", "message": "..." }

    to the bridge’s /send endpoint:

    app.post('/send', async (req, res) => {
      const { chatId, message } = req.body;
      const sent = await sock.sendMessage(chatId, { text: prefixed });
      ...
    });
```

  • Baileys attempts to decode chatId as a JID and fails, producing:

    Cannot destructure property 'user' of 'jidDecode(...)' as it is undefined.
  • Cron therefore logs a delivery error, and the user never sees the message on WhatsApp, despite the job itself having succeeded.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

WhatsApp

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

0.4.0 (2026.06.18)

### Relevant Logs / Traceback

```shell
.hermes/logs/errors.log

2026-03-18 13:24:35,109 ERROR cron.scheduler: Job '9cc2b836678f': delivery error: WhatsApp bridge error (500): {"error":"Cannot destructure property 'user' of 'jidDecode(...)' as it is undefined."}
2026-03-18 13:44:34,664 ERROR cron.scheduler: Job '9cc2b836678f': delivery error: WhatsApp bridge error (500): {"error":"Cannot destructure property 'user' of 'jidDecode(...)' as it is undefined."}
2026-03-18 14:00:33,347 ERROR cron.scheduler: Job '315e6f2a8f57': delivery error: WhatsApp bridge error (500): {"error":"Cannot destructure property 'user' of 'jidDecode(...)' as it is undefined."}
2026-03-18 14:30:09,169 ERROR cron.scheduler: Job '9cc2b836678f': delivery error: WhatsApp bridge error (500): {"error":"Cannot destructure property 'user' of 'jidDecode(...)' as it is undefined."}
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

_No response_

### Proposed Fix (optional)

 1. Enhance `_resolve_delivery_target()` in `cron/scheduler.py` to resolve human-friendly names via the channel directory, mirroring send_message behavior.

     Example logic:

     from gateway.channel_directory import resolve_channel_name
```
     if ":" in deliver:
         platform_name, target_ref = deliver.split(":", 1)
         platform_name = platform_name.strip()
         target_ref = target_ref.strip()
         # Strip display suffixes like " (dm)" / " (group)"
         normalized = target_ref
         if normalized.endswith(")") and " (" in normalized:
             normalized = normalized.rsplit(" (", 1)[0].strip()
         resolved = None
         try:
             resolved = resolve_channel_name(platform_name.lower(), normalized)
         except Exception:
             resolved = None
         return {
             "platform": platform_name,
             "chat_id": resolved or target_ref,
             "thread_id": None,
         }
```

     This preserves compatibility:
    • If deliver is already a raw JID (e.g. whatsapp:12345678901234@lid), resolve_channel_name will typically return None, and the code falls back to using target_ref unchanged.
  2. Clarify the docs for `deliver`, explicitly stating the supported formats and how name-based targets are resolved for WhatsApp.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR


### Workaround: 

What works, but is pretty hacky is following code changes: 

```
git diff cron/scheduler.py tools/send_message_tool.py
diff --git a/cron/scheduler.py b/cron/scheduler.py
index ea7ff0e9..f8476ef3 100644
--- a/cron/scheduler.py
+++ b/cron/scheduler.py
@@ -80,10 +80,31 @@ def _resolve_delivery_target(job: dict) -> Optional[dict]:
         }

     if ":" in deliver:
-        platform_name, chat_id = deliver.split(":", 1)
+        platform_name, target_ref = deliver.split(":", 1)
+        platform_name = platform_name.strip()
+        target_ref = target_ref.strip()
+
+        # Cron delivery often gets configured using the human-friendly
+        # labels from `send_message(action="list")`, e.g.:
+        #   "whatsapp:Daniel Andersen (dm)"
+        # Those labels are not valid WhatsApp JIDs; resolve them via the
+        # channel directory so the bridge receives a real "<number>@lid".
+        resolved = None
+        try:
+            from gateway.channel_directory import resolve_channel_name
+
+            normalized = target_ref
+            if normalized.endswith(")") and " (" in normalized:
+                # Strip display suffix like "(dm)" or "(group)"
+                normalized = normalized.rsplit(" (", 1)[0].strip()
+
+            resolved = resolve_channel_name(platform_name.lower(), normalized)
+        except Exception:
+            resolved = None
+
         return {
             "platform": platform_name,
-            "chat_id": chat_id,
+            "chat_id": resolved or target_ref,
             "thread_id": None,
         }

diff --git a/tools/send_message_tool.py b/tools/send_message_tool.py
index 3ebd6c5b..eb6cb6ff 100644
--- a/tools/send_message_tool.py
+++ b/tools/send_message_tool.py
@@ -94,7 +94,13 @@ def _handle_send(args):
     if target_ref and not is_explicit:
         try:
             from gateway.channel_directory import resolve_channel_name
-            resolved = resolve_channel_name(platform_name, target_ref)
+            normalized = target_ref
+            # WhatsApp list entries often include display suffixes like " (dm)".
+            # The directory stores the plain name without that suffix.
+            if platform_name == "whatsapp" and normalized.endswith(")") and " (" in normalized:
+                normalized = normalized.rsplit(" (", 1)[0].strip()
+
+            resolved = resolve_channel_name(platform_name, normalized)
             if resolved:
                 chat_id, thread_id, _ = _parse_target_ref(platform_name, resolved)
             else:
@@ -194,6 +200,26 @@ def _parse_target_ref(platform_name: str, target_ref: str):
         match = _TELEGRAM_TOPIC_TARGET_RE.fullmatch(target_ref)
         if match:
             return match.group(1), match.group(2), True
+
+    # WhatsApp: accept direct JIDs (e.g. "<number>@lid") and also convert bare
+    # numbers ("<number>"/"+<number>") to "<number>@<suffix>" using the configured
+    # home channel (WHATSAPP_HOME_CHANNEL).
+    if platform_name == "whatsapp":
+        t = (target_ref or "").strip()
+
+        # Direct JID-like target
+        if "@" in t:
+            return t, None, True
+
+        # Bare phone number / digits
+        t_digits = t[1:] if t.startswith("+") else t
+        if t_digits.isdigit():
+            home = os.getenv("WHATSAPP_HOME_CHANNEL", "").strip()
+            if "@" in home:
+                suffix = home.split("@", 1)[1]
+                return f"{t_digits}@{suffix}", None, True
+            return t_digits, None, True
+
     if target_ref.lstrip("-").isdigit():
         return target_ref, None, True
     return None, None, False

items.body:
## Bug Description

After PR #1675 removed `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` env var support, the Anthropic provider base URL is hardcoded to `https://api.anthropic.com` in two places:

1. **`hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py`** (line 313) — main runtime resolution
2. **`agent/auxiliary_client.py`** `_try_anthropic()` (line 659) — auxiliary client

This makes it impossible to use Anthropic-compatible proxies (Sub2API, LiteLLM proxy, etc.) without modifying source code.

## Expected Behavior

The Anthropic provider should respect `model.base_url` from `config.yaml`, consistent with how other providers (alibaba, custom, etc.) handle base URL overrides.

```yaml
# config.yaml
model:
  provider: anthropic
  base_url: http://localhost:8080  # should be respected
```

## Current Behavior

The `base_url` field is completely ignored for the Anthropic provider. It always resolves to `https://api.anthropic.com`.

items.title: feat: per-channel model and system prompt overrides for gateway platforms
items.body:
## Use Case

In a Discord server (or Telegram group), different channels often serve different purposes:

- **#daily** — low-cost summarization channel using a free/cheap model (e.g. `openrouter/healer-alpha`)
- **#dev** — coding assistant channel using a capable model (e.g. `anthropic/claude-opus-4.6`)
- **#casual** — general chat with a different persona/system prompt

Currently, the gateway uses a single global model + system prompt for **all** channels. Users who need per-channel differentiation must run separate bot instances or use an external routing layer.

## Proposed Design

Add a `channel_overrides` section under each platform config in `config.yaml`:

```yaml
platforms:
  discord:
    enabled: true
    channel_overrides:
      "1234567890":           # channel ID
        model: openrouter/healer-alpha
        provider: openrouter
        system_prompt: "You are a daily news summarizer."
      "9876543210":
        model: anthropic/claude-opus-4.6
        provider: anthropic
        system_prompt: "You are a coding assistant."
```

### Resolution priority (high → low):

1. `/model` command (ephemeral, per-session)
2. `channel_overrides[channel_id]` (persistent, per-channel)
3. `model.default` / `agent.system_prompt` (global fallback)

### Implementation scope:

1. **`gateway/config.py`** — extend `PlatformConfig` with `channel_overrides: Dict[str, ChannelOverride]`
2. **`gateway/run.py`** — `_resolve_gateway_model()` and `_load_ephemeral_system_prompt()` accept `chat_id` parameter, check overrides before global config
3. **Agent construction** — pass resolved model/provider/system_prompt per dispatch

### What it does NOT change:

- No changes to CLI mode
- No changes to the agent loop or prompt caching
- Channels without overrides behave exactly as today

## Alternatives Considered

- **Multiple bot instances**: works but wastes resources, hard to manage
- **External routing proxy**: adds latency and complexity
- **Personality system** (`/personality`): exists but is per-session, not per-channel, and does not support model overrides

## Prior Art

Other agent frameworks (e.g. OpenClaw) support `modelByChannel` config and it is a commonly requested feature for multi-channel deployments.

items.title: [Feature]: Observation masking for older turns: reduce conversation history tokens without LLM summarization
items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

In multi-turn agent conversations, tool outputs (file reads, terminal output, web search results) from earlier turns are re-sent in full with every API call. This causes quadratic token growth — by turn 10, the context can contain thousands of tokens of stale tool output that the agent will never reference again.

The current `context_compressor.py` uses LLM-based summarization when context exceeds limits. This works but:
- Costs extra tokens (the summarization call itself)
- Adds latency (extra API round-trip)
- Can lose important details

JetBrains Research published "The Complexity Trap" (NeurIPS 2025 DL4Code workshop, arXiv:2508.21433) showing that **simple observation masking** — replacing old tool outputs with a short placeholder like `[output hidden, N chars]` — achieves the **same performance as LLM summarization** at 52.7% cost reduction, with zero extra API calls.


### Proposed Solution

Add observation masking as a lightweight first-pass in `context_compressor.py`, before the existing LLM summarization kicks in.

Config option:

  context:
    observation_masking: true          # default: true
    observation_masking_window: 4      # keep last N turns unmasked

Behavior:
1. For turns older than the masking window, replace tool/function result content with: `[observation masked — {N} chars, use session_search to recall if needed]`
2. Keep the agent's own reasoning and actions (assistant messages) intact — only mask environment observations
3. The existing LLM summarization remains as a second-pass safety net for when context still exceeds limits after masking

This is complementary to the existing compression — masking handles the common case cheaply, summarization handles edge cases.

Reference: https://blog.jetbrains.com/research/2025/12/efficient-context-management/
Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.21433


### Alternatives Considered

1. **LLM summarization only** (current approach) — works but costs extra tokens and adds latency. The JetBrains research shows masking is equally effective.
2. **Aggressive context truncation** — risks losing important context. Masking is more surgical — it only hides verbose tool outputs while preserving the agent's reasoning chain.
3. **Hybrid masking + summarization** — the JetBrains paper shows this can be even more effective. The proposed implementation supports this naturally since masking runs first and summarization remains as fallback.


### Feature Type

Performance / reliability

### Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

items.title: [Bug] webapi/deps.py import mismatch (_resolve_model vs _resolve_gateway_model) breaks local model routing in Docker
items.body:
## Bug Report

**What happened:**
When running the Hermes Workspace Docker setup with a local llama.cpp server, the web UI gets stuck on "Thinking..." indefinitely with no error message.

**Root cause:**
In webapi/deps.py, the import tries to load _resolve_model from gateway.run, but that function does not exist there — it is called _resolve_gateway_model. The import fails silently, so Hermes falls back to a basic resolver that drops base_url entirely and sends all requests to the default provider instead of your local endpoint.

**Impact:**
Anyone using local models (llama.cpp, Ollama, vLLM) via the Docker/web UI is affected. No error is shown — it just silently fails and hangs forever.

**Suggested fix:**
Rename the import in webapi/deps.py from _resolve_model to _resolve_gateway_model.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Run the Hermes Workspace Docker container
2. Configure a local llama.cpp server on port 8080
3. Set OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:8080/v1 and OPENAI_API_KEY=dummy
4. Open the web UI and send a message — hangs on "Thinking..." indefinitely
5. Check Docker logs — fallback resolver is used and base_url is missing

**Note:**
This bug is in the outsourc-e/hermes-agent fork used by the hermes-workspace Docker setup. Reporting here since the fork has issues disabled.

**Environment:**
- Windows 11 + WSL2
- llama.cpp on port 8080
- Hermes Workspace UI via Docker

### Bug Description

## Summary

The `hermes sessions list` command truncates session IDs to 20 characters, but the full session ID is 24 characters. This makes it impossible to copy the correct ID for `hermes --resume`.


## Impact

- **Severity**: Medium
- **User Impact**: Users cannot resume sessions using IDs from `hermes sessions list`
- **Workaround**: Use `hermes --resume` with the ID shown at exit, or use `hermes sessions browse` for interactive selection

## Related Code

- Session ID generation: `cli.py:1176`
- Session ID display at exit: `cli.py:5580`
- Session list command: `hermes_cli/main.py:3717-3738`


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a Hermes CLI session
2. Exit the session — you see:
   ```
   Resume this session with:
     hermes --resume 20260319_142635_a4ec9f
   ```
3. Run `hermes sessions list`
4. Observe the ID column shows only `20260319_142635_a4ec` (missing last 2 characters)


### Expected Behavior

The ID column in `hermes sessions list` should display the full session ID:
```
20260319_142635_a4ec9f  (24 characters)
```


### Actual Behavior

The ID column shows a truncated ID:

20260319_142635_a4ec    (20 characters, last 2 chars missing)

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

File: `hermes_cli/main.py`
Lines: 3734, 3737

```python
# Line 3734 (when sessions have titles)

# Line 3737 (when sessions don't have titles)

```

Session IDs are generated in `cli.py` line 1176:

# Format: YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_aaaaaa

```

The `[:20]` slice truncates the last 4 characters of the ID.


### Proposed Fix (optional)

Change lines 3734 and 3737 in `hermes_cli/main.py`:

```python
# Option 1: Show full ID (recommended)
sid = s["id"]  # Remove the [:20] truncation

# Option 2: Increase width to 24 characters
sid = s["id"][:24]
```

Also adjust the table format string on lines 3724 and 3727 to accommodate the wider ID column:

```python
# Line 3724: Change from {'ID'} to {'ID':<24}
print(f"{'Title':<22} {'Preview':<40} {'Last Active':<13} {'ID':<24}")

items.title: delegate_task saves child's tool names instead of parent's (post-mutation timing bug)
items.body:
## Bug: `_run_single_child` saves the wrong tool-name state

### Version
Current `main` at `04b6ecad` (post-fix for #1802 via #1804 / #1894)

### Relationship to #1802
Issue #1802 reported a `NameError` where `_saved_tool_names` was defined in `_build_child_agent()` but referenced in `_run_single_child()`. That scope bug was fixed by commits `ba7248c6` and `ae8059ca`, which moved the save into `_run_single_child()`. The NameError is gone, but the save now captures the **wrong value** — the child's tool names instead of the parent's.

### Root Cause

The execution flow creates a timing bug:

1. `delegate_task()` calls `_build_child_agent()` on the main thread (L471)
2. Inside, `AIAgent()` constructor calls `get_tool_definitions()` (`run_agent.py` L757)
3. `get_tool_definitions()` **overwrites** the process-global `model_tools._last_resolved_tool_names` with the **child's** toolset (`model_tools.py` L291-292)
4. `_run_single_child()` then runs and saves the global at L270:
   ```python
   _saved_tool_names = list(model_tools._last_resolved_tool_names)
   ```
   This is now the **child's** tool names, not the parent's.

5. The `finally` block at L384-386 "restores" the child's tools back — a no-op at best.

### Impact

**Single task mode:** After `delegate_task` returns, `_last_resolved_tool_names` contains the child's toolset instead of the parent's. Any downstream consumer of this global (e.g. `execute_code` sandbox tool filtering at `model_tools.py` L356) sees the wrong tool list.

**Batch mode (additional issue):** All children are built sequentially on the main thread before any worker thread starts. Each `_build_child_agent()` call overwrites the global. Then worker threads race to save/restore the same global with no coordination:
- Thread A saves → Thread B saves (overwrites A's save) → Thread A restores B's value
- No authoritative main-thread restore after `ThreadPoolExecutor` completes (L488-541)
- The final state of `_last_resolved_tool_names` is whichever thread's `finally` ran last — nondeterministic.

### Reproduction

```python
# Simplified flow showing the bug:
import model_tools

# Parent has these tools
model_tools._last_resolved_tool_names = ["terminal", "read_file", "delegate_task", "memory"]

# _build_child_agent() constructs AIAgent(), which calls get_tool_definitions()
# This overwrites the global with the child's restricted toolset:
model_tools._last_resolved_tool_names = ["terminal", "read_file"]  # child's tools

# _run_single_child() saves the global — but it's already the child's tools
_saved_tool_names = list(model_tools._last_resolved_tool_names)
# _saved_tool_names == ["terminal", "read_file"]  ← WRONG, should be parent's

# After restore, parent's "memory" and "delegate_task" are lost
```

### Why Existing Tests Don't Catch It

The regression tests added in `ae8059ca` (from PR #2038) test that `_delegate_saved_tool_names` is set and restored, but they mock `AIAgent()` construction so `get_tool_definitions()` never actually runs — the global is never mutated during the test, masking the timing issue.

### Suggested Approach

Save the parent's tool names **before** any child construction mutates the global, either:
- At the top of `delegate_task()` before the `_build_child_agent()` loop
- Passed through to `_run_single_child` via the child object or parameter
- With an authoritative main-thread restore after all futures complete (critical for batch mode)

items.title: Feature: Add discord_fetch_message tool
items.body:
## Feature Description

Add support for fetching Discord messages by ID via a `discord_fetch_message` tool.

## Motivation

Hermes currently cannot access Discord message history. When users paste Discord message links (e.g., `https://discord.com/channels/1472019441586933937/1484330055529136158/1484330123011428442`), Hermes can parse the link but cannot retrieve the actual message content. This limits conversation continuity and context awareness.

## Proposed Solution

### Implementation Plan

1. **Expose Discord client to tools layer**
   - The Discord gateway adapter already has a Discord bot client
   - Make it accessible to the tool system

2. **Create `discord_fetch_message` tool**
   - File: `tools/discord_tool.py`
   - Parameters:
     - `message_id` (str, required): Discord message ID
     - `channel_id` (str, optional): Channel ID (if inferable from context)
   - Returns: Message content, author, timestamp, attachments

3. **Register the tool**
   - Add to `tools/registry.py`
   - Add to appropriate toolset in `toolsets.py`
   - Check that bot has "Read Message History" permission

4. **Gateway integration**
   - Ensure the Discord client is available to the tool handler
   - May need to pass the client through a singleton or dependency injection

### Example Usage

```
User: https://discord.com/channels/1472019441586933937/1484330055529136158/1484330123011428442
Hermes: [Parses link] Fetching message 1484330123011428442 from channel 1484330055529136158...
Hermes: Found! User @diegohb said: "Here's the config we discussed earlier: [...]"
```

## Technical Notes

- Discord API: `GET /channels/{channel.id}/messages/{message.id}`
- Bot must be in the server and have access to the channel
- Rate limits: ~50 requests per second per bot (should be fine for Hermes use)
- Error handling: 404 (message deleted), 403 (no access), etc.

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Search session history** - Already works for past Hermes conversations, but not for messages Hermes wasn't present for
2. **User manual paste** - Works but cumbersome, defeats the purpose of link references
3. **Full Discord history dump** - Overkill, privacy concerns

## Labels

enhancement, discord, tool, feature

items.title: [Bug]: Quiet mode with --resume does not pass conversation history to LLM
items.body:
### Describe the bug

When using `hermes chat -q "message" --quiet --resume SESSION_ID`, the session is loaded correctly (`_init_agent()` populates `cli.conversation_history` from SQLite and prints the correct message counts), but the conversation history is never passed to `run_conversation()`. The LLM responds without any prior context.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `hermes chat -q "My name is Alice" --quiet` — note the `session_id`
2. `hermes chat -q "What is my name?" --quiet --resume <session_id>`
3. Agent prints "Resumed session ... (1 user message, N total messages)" but responds as if it has no prior context

### Expected behavior

The agent should respond with awareness of the prior conversation (e.g., "Your name is Alice").

### Root cause

In `cli.py` line 7099, the quiet-mode code path calls:
```python
result = cli.agent.run_conversation(query)
```

This does not pass `conversation_history`, so `run_conversation()` defaults to an empty list. The interactive mode at line 5347 correctly passes it:
```python
result = self.agent.run_conversation(
    user_message=agent_message,
    conversation_history=self.conversation_history[:-1],
)
```

### Fix

Change line 7099 to:
```python
result = cli.agent.run_conversation(
    user_message=query,
    conversation_history=cli.conversation_history,
)
```

(The full list is passed without `[:-1]` because the current user message has not been appended to `conversation_history` in the quiet-mode code path.)

### Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04
- Python: 3.12
- Hermes: main branch (as of 2026-03-19)

## Bug Description

Commit `e84d952d` ("fix(codex): handle reasoning-only responses and replay path #2070") adds an empty assistant message after reasoning-only responses to satisfy the Responses API `missing_following_item` requirement:

```python
# run_agent.py, _chat_messages_to_responses_input()
items.append({"role": "assistant", "content": ""})
```

This empty assistant message persists in the conversation history and gets sent on subsequent turns to **any** provider — including the Chat Completions API path and Anthropic Messages API providers that reject trailing assistant messages as unsupported prefill.

## Reproduction

1. Use Hermes with `provider: litellm` (or any OpenAI-compatible custom endpoint) routing to a mix of models
2. Have a thinking model (e.g. MiniMax M2.5, Kimi K2.5) return a reasoning-only response (only `reasoning_content`, no visible `content`)
3. The empty assistant message gets appended to conversation history
4. Next user message triggers a request with messages ending in: `...user → assistant("") → user`
5. The provider rejects with: `"This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message."`

## Error Message

```
litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - This model does not support assistant message prefill. 
The conversation must end with a user message.
```

This also occurs with Anthropic Messages API when using OAuth tokens (Claude Max subscriptions via CLIProxyAPI), which explicitly reject prefill.

## Impact

- Affects any multi-model setup where thinking models coexist with non-thinking models
- Affects Claude Max subscription users routing through OpenAI-compatible proxies
- The empty assistant message is invisible to the user but breaks subsequent API calls
- The error repeats on every subsequent message until the session is reset

## Root Cause

The fix in `_chat_messages_to_responses_input()` correctly handles the Responses API requirement, but the empty assistant message should either:

1. Be stripped before sending to non-Responses-API providers (Chat Completions / Messages API)
2. Be tagged as Responses-API-specific so it does not get included in Chat Completions API requests
3. Be cleaned up from the conversation history after the Responses API turn completes

## Workaround

LiteLLM custom callback that strips trailing empty assistant messages:

```python
class StripPrefillCallback(CustomLogger):
    async def async_pre_call_hook(self, user_api_key_dict, cache, data, call_type):
        messages = data.get("messages", [])
        if messages and messages[-1].get("role") == "assistant":
            content = messages[-1].get("content", "")
            if not content or len(str(content)) < 50:
                data["messages"] = messages[:-1]
        return data
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: commit `4c0c7f4c` (post-update including `e84d952d`)
- LiteLLM proxy with OpenAI-compatible endpoints
- Thinking models (MiniMax, Kimi) producing reasoning-only responses
- Claude Max via CLIProxyAPI (OAuth-based, rejects prefill)

items.title: Bug: session_count() and message_count() missing thread lock
items.body:
## Bug Description

`SessionDB` in `hermes_state.py` explicitly promises thread-safety (line 111):

> Thread-safe for the common gateway pattern (multiple reader threads, single writer via WAL mode). Each method opens its own cursor.

Every database-accessing method in the class (22 total) wraps operations in `with self._lock:` — **except** `session_count()` (line 856) and `message_count()` (line 866), which access `self._conn` without any lock.

## Code

```python
def session_count(self, source: str = None) -> int:
    """Count sessions, optionally filtered by source."""
    if source:
        cursor = self._conn.execute(
            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions WHERE source = ?", (source,)
        )
    else:
        cursor = self._conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions")
    return cursor.fetchone()[0]

def message_count(self, session_id: str = None) -> int:
    """Count messages, optionally for a specific session."""
    if session_id:
        cursor = self._conn.execute(
            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE session_id = ?", (session_id,)
        )
    else:
        cursor = self._conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages")
    return cursor.fetchone()[0]
```

## Impact

In the gateway's multi-threaded environment (multiple platform reader threads + writer), concurrent access to `self._conn` without the lock can cause:

- Race conditions during reads (cursor interleaving)
- `sqlite3.ProgrammingError` if the connection is used concurrently
- Inconsistent results from `fetchone()` on a shared connection

## Proposed Fix

Wrap both methods with `with self._lock:`, matching the pattern used by all other methods in the class.

## Environment

- File: `hermes_state.py`, lines 856–874
- Class: `SessionDB`

items.title: fix(toolsets): resolve_toolset() uses visited.copy() preventing cross-branch deduplication
items.body:
## Bug Description

`resolve_toolset()` in `toolsets.py` (line 375) passes `visited.copy()` when recursing into included toolsets. This creates a fresh visited set for each include branch, which means:

1. **Diamond dependencies are resolved multiple times.** If toolsets B and C both include D, D is resolved twice instead of once.
2. **Duplicate cycle warnings.** For cycles like A→[B,C], B→C, C→B — the cycle warning fires once per path instead of once total.
3. **Exponential blowup potential.** With deep diamond dependency trees, each level doubles the work since sibling branches don't share their visited sets.

## Reproduction

```python
from toolsets import TOOLSETS, resolve_toolset

# Branching cycle: A → [B, C], B → C, C → B
TOOLSETS['_a'] = {'description': 'test', 'tools': ['t1'], 'includes': ['_b', '_c']}
TOOLSETS['_b'] = {'description': 'test', 'tools': ['t2'], 'includes': ['_c']}
TOOLSETS['_c'] = {'description': 'test', 'tools': ['t3'], 'includes': ['_b']}

resolve_toolset('_a')
# Prints TWO warnings instead of one:
# ⚠️  Circular dependency detected in toolset '_b'
# ⚠️  Circular dependency detected in toolset '_c'
```

## Proposed Fix

1. Remove `.copy()` on line 375 — pass `visited` directly so sibling includes share the set
2. Keep `.copy()` on line 354 (the `"all"`/`"*"` alias) — each top-level toolset should be resolved independently
3. Remove the misleading `print()` warning — with a shared visited set, hitting a visited name can mean either a diamond (not a bug) or a cycle; silently returning `[]` is correct in both cases since tools are collected into a set

## Environment

- File: `toolsets.py`, lines 358–375
- Function: `resolve_toolset()`

## Bug Description

Two resource management issues in `code_execution_tool.py`:

### 1. Resource leak in RPC stdout/stderr suppression (lines 301-315)

Two separate `open(os.devnull, "w")` calls are made on lines 303-304. If an exception occurs after the first `open()` succeeds but before the inner `try` block, the first file handle leaks because the `finally` block (line 309-312) is scoped to the inner `try`.

```python
sys.stdout = open(os.devnull, "w")   # succeeds
sys.stderr = open(os.devnull, "w")   # if this throws, first handle leaks

2. Set `server_sock = None` after the first close to prevent the double close in finally.

items.title: fix(cron): unawaited coroutine when asyncio.run() hits RuntimeError
items.body:
## Bug Description

In `cron/scheduler.py` (lines 159-167), when `asyncio.run()` raises `RuntimeError` (because an event loop is already running), the coroutine object passed to it is never awaited or closed:

```python
try:
    result = asyncio.run(_send_to_platform(...))  # coroutine created here
except RuntimeError:
    # coroutine from line 160 is abandoned — never awaited
    import concurrent.futures
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as pool:
        future = pool.submit(asyncio.run, _send_to_platform(...))  # NEW coroutine
        result = future.result(timeout=30)
```

`asyncio.run()` checks for a running event loop *before* awaiting the coroutine. When it raises, the coroutine is abandoned and triggers `RuntimeWarning: coroutine '_send_to_platform' was never awaited` on garbage collection.

## Proposed Fix

Create the coroutine before the try block and explicitly close it in the except path:

```python
coro = _send_to_platform(...)
try:
    result = asyncio.run(coro)
except RuntimeError:
    coro.close()  # prevent RuntimeWarning
    ...
```

## Environment

- File: `cron/scheduler.py`, lines 158-167

items.title: Bug: Context compression fails to trigger on API disconnect, causing death spiral in gateway sessions
items.body:
## Bug Report

### Description

Gateway (Telegram) sessions can grow to 212k+ tokens / 700+ messages, causing Anthropic API connection failures ("Server disconnected without sending a response"). Three layers of compression defense all fail simultaneously, creating an unrecoverable death spiral.

**Model:** claude-opus-4.6 with 200k context limit
**Config:** compression threshold = 0.85 (170k tokens trigger point)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a gateway (Telegram) session with claude-opus-4.6
2. Accumulate a long conversation history approaching the 200k context limit
3. Context grows past the limit, causing API disconnect
4. Send another message — session never recovers

### Expected Behavior

When the API disconnects due to oversized context, compression should be triggered automatically before the next retry or message, bringing the context back within limits.

### Actual Behavior

API disconnects → no usage data saved → compression not triggered → next message reloads same bloated history → API disconnects again → repeat forever. User must manually delete the session to recover.

### Root Cause Analysis

Three defense layers exist, and all three fail simultaneously:

**Layer 1: Agent in-loop compression (`run_agent.py` line 6487)**
- Checks `should_compress()` after each tool call
- Relies on `last_prompt_tokens` from the previous API response usage data
- **FAILURE:** When API disconnects due to oversized context, no usage data is returned, so `last_prompt_tokens` stays at its old (stale) value. `should_compress()` never triggers.

**Layer 2: Preflight compression (`run_agent.py` line 5245)**
- Runs once at start of `run_conversation()` using rough estimate (`len(str(msg))//4`)
- **FAILURE:** Only runs once at entry. If tools within a single conversation turn inflate context past the limit, this does not re-check.

**Layer 3: Gateway Session Hygiene (`gateway/run.py` lines 1636-1834)**
- Pre-agent check when Telegram message arrives
- Uses `session_entry.last_prompt_tokens` (real API value) when available, falls back to rough estimate with 1.4x safety factor on threshold
- Hygiene threshold = 0.85 x 200k = 170k
- **FAILURE:** When previous agent call disconnected without returning usage, `last_prompt_tokens` = 0. Falls back to rough estimate mode. But the rough estimate with 1.4x inflated threshold (238k) makes it HARDER to trigger, not easier — the direction is inverted. The 1.4x factor was meant to compensate for rough estimate overestimation on tool-heavy content, but it makes the safety net less sensitive.

### Key Files Involved

- `agent/context_compressor.py` — ContextCompressor class, should_compress(), compress()
- `run_agent.py` lines 5235-5270 (preflight), 6479-6492 (in-loop check)
- `gateway/run.py` lines 1636-1834 (session hygiene)
- `agent/model_metadata.py` line 793 — estimate_messages_tokens_rough()

### Suggested Fixes

1. **API error handler compression:** In the API connection error catch block, use rough estimate to proactively trigger compression before retry
2. **Fix gateway hygiene threshold direction:** The 1.4x factor inflates the THRESHOLD (making it less sensitive) — it should deflate the threshold or inflate the estimate instead
3. **Hard message count safety valve:** If messages > 500, force compression regardless of token estimates
4. **Persistent token tracking:** Store a "last known good" prompt_tokens that persists even when API calls fail, so subsequent checks are not blind

### Environment

- Model: claude-opus-4.6 (200k context limit)
- Platform: Telegram gateway
- Compression threshold config: 0.85

items.title: Feature: @-mention-only mode for Mattermost gateway adapter
items.body:
## Summary

Add a configurable option to the Mattermost gateway adapter to only respond when @-mentioned in channels/groups, while always processing DMs.

## Motivation

In multi-user channels, the bot currently processes **every** message from other users. This creates noise and unnecessary API calls. Most messaging platforms (Discord, Slack) already filter for mentions in their adapters — Mattermost should have parity.

## Proposed behavior

- **DMs** (`channel_type == "D"`): Always processed (no change)
- **Channels/groups**: Only processed if the bot is @-mentioned
  - Check `post["mentions"]` list for bot's user ID
  - Fallback: check message text for `@username` or `<@user_id>`
  - Also respond to `@channel`, `@all`, `@here` broadcast mentions

## Implementation

In `gateway/platforms/mattermost.py` `_handle_post()`, after the self-message filter, add:

\`\`\`python
# Mention-only mode: skip channel messages that don't @mention the bot.
# DMs (type "D") are always processed.
channel_type_raw = data.get("channel_type", "O")
if channel_type_raw != "D":
    # Check structured mentions field first
    mentions = post.get("mentions", [])
    if isinstance(mentions, str):
        mentions = mentions.split(",")
    has_mention = self._bot_user_id in mentions if mentions else False

    # Fallback: check message text for @username or @user_id
    if not has_mention:
        mention_patterns = [f"@{self._bot_username}", f"@{self._bot_user_id}"]
        has_mention = any(p.lower() in message.lower() for p in mention_patterns)

    # Also respond to broadcast mentions
    if not has_mention:
        has_mention = any(m in message for m in ("@channel", "@all", "@here"))

    if not has_mention:
        return
\`\`\`

## Configuration option (optional)

A `MATTERMOST_MENTION_ONLY` env var (default: `true`) could gate this behavior for backwards compatibility.

## Context

This has been running as a local patch in production on a hermes-agent Docker deployment and works well. The structured `mentions` field from the WebSocket `posted` event reliably contains the bot's user ID when mentioned.

## Related

Parity with Discord and Slack adapters which already filter for mentions.

items.title: [BUG] `hermes gateway run --replace` fails when old gateway process is STOPPED (Ctrl+Z)
items.body:
## Summary
`hermes gateway run --replace` exits silently with code 0 when a previous gateway process was suspended (Ctrl+Z / SIGTSTP) instead of properly killed. The gateway appears to start but immediately exits without any error message.

## Root Cause
The `--replace` flag properly:
1. Checks for running gateway via PID file (`get_running_pid()`)
2. Kills the process and removes the PID file
3. Writes a new PID file

HOWEVER, there are two issues:

### Issue 1: Stopped processes are not detected
When a gateway process is STOPPED (Ctrl+Z / SIGTSTP) but not killed:
- The PID file may be empty/stale
- `get_running_pid()` returns `None` (no running gateway detected)
- The new gateway starts
- Platform adapters (e.g., Telegram) try to acquire scoped locks via `acquire_scoped_lock()`
- `os.kill(stopped_pid, 0)` **succeeds** because stopped processes still exist
- Lock acquisition fails → gateway exits with misleading error

### Issue 2: Scoped locks are not released
The `--replace` logic in `start_gateway()` removes the PID file but does NOT release scoped locks in `~/.local/state/hermes/gateway-locks/`. These lock files persist with stale PIDs.

## Evidence
```bash
# Gateway.log shows the real error:
2026-03-20 21:00:34,660 ERROR gateway.platforms.telegram: [Telegram] Another local Hermes gateway is already using this Telegram bot token (PID 2700844). Stop the other gateway before starting a second Telegram poller.

# But the process was STOPPED, not running:
$ cat /proc/2700844/status | grep State
State:   T (stopped)

# Scoped lock file still existed:
$ cat ~/.local/state/hermes/gateway-locks/telegram-bot-token-*.lock
{
  "pid": 2700844,
  "kind": "hermes-gateway",
  "argv": ["/home/stefanu/.local/bin/hermes", "gateway", "run", "--replace"],
  "start_time": 17476067,
  "scope": "telegram-bot-token",
  ...
}

# PID file was empty:
$ cat ~/.hermes/gateway.pid
(empty)

# Process state showed it was stopped (Tl = sleeping, thread count; T = stopped):
$ ps aux | grep 2700844
stefanu  2700844  0.0  1.2 680752 208392 pts/2   Tl   15:22   0:23 ...hermes gateway run --replace
```

## Impact
- User runs `hermes gateway run --replace` and sees success banner
- Gateway exits immediately with no error message
- Exit code is 0 (success), so systemd cannot auto-restart
- Confusing UX — user has no idea what went wrong

## Reproduction
1. Start gateway: `hermes gateway run`
2. Suspend it: `Ctrl+Z`
3. Try to replace: `hermes gateway run --replace`
4. Gateway shows startup banner but exits immediately with no error

## Suggested Fix
Two options:

### Option A: Release scoped locks in `--replace` logic
In `gateway/run.py` `start_gateway()` function, after killing the old process:
```python
# After line 5077 (remove_pid_file()):
# Also release all scoped locks
from gateway.status import release_all_scoped_locks
release_all_scoped_locks()
```

Would need to add a new function `release_all_scoped_locks()` in `gateway/status.py` that removes all lock files in `_get_lock_dir()`.

### Option B: Check process state in `acquire_scoped_lock()`
In `gateway/status.py` `acquire_scoped_lock()`, check if the process is actually running (not just stopped):
```python
# Around line 265-268, after os.kill(pid, 0) succeeds:
# Check process state via /proc/<pid>/status
state = _get_process_state(existing_pid)
if state in ("T",):  # stopped
    stale = True  # Treat stopped processes as stale
```

### Option C: Both
Implement both fixes for defense in depth.

## Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.4.0 (2026.3.18)
- Python 3.11.14
- WSL2 on Windows
- Ubuntu (Linux)

## Workaround
Kill all gateway processes manually and remove lock files:
```bash
pkill -9 -f "hermes.*gateway"
rm -f ~/.local/state/hermes/gateway-locks/*.lock
rm -f ~/.hermes/gateway.pid
```

items.title: Feature: Richer local memory — structured retrieval and fact extraction beyond flat files
items.body:
## Summary

Hermes has memory built in and it works — the `memory` tool saves facts to `~/.hermes/` and `session_search` gives cross-session recall. For basic use that's fine.

But the backend is flat files with no retrieval intelligence. As memory grows, you get:

- No semantic search — recall is keyword/FTS only, misses conceptually related memories
- No fact extraction — raw text is stored as-is, no structure or deduplication
- No entity resolution — "the user" and "Ben" are unrelated entries
- No relevance ranking — older or less relevant memories surface equally

## What better local memory looks like

A richer local backend would store structured facts, resolve entities, and rank results by relevance — all running locally, no cloud dependency.

[`hindsight-hermes`](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight/tree/main/hindsight-integrations/hermes) is a working example of this via the plugin system. It runs fully locally via Docker and gives Hermes structured fact extraction, entity resolution, and multi-strategy retrieval (semantic + BM25 + graph). PR #1811 is the integration.

The ask here is for this kind of capability to be accessible without needing an external plugin — either as a first-class memory backend option or by making the current backend more pluggable so alternatives are easier to drop in.

## Related

- #346 Structured Memory System
- #674 Memory Storage Migration  
- #677 Semantic Memory Recall

When sending messages containing backslashes inside code spans (inline `` ` `` or fenced `` ``` ``), the backslashes are silently consumed by Telegram's MarkdownV2 parser and do not render in the client.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Send a message via Telegram gateway containing an inline code Windows path:
```

```
2. Observe the rendered message in Telegram


### Expected Behavior

The backslashes render as literal characters:
```

```

### Actual Behavior

Backslashes are consumed — the path renders as:
```

```

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS

Python 3.12.10

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

In `gateway/platforms/telegram.py`, `format_message()` extracts code entities into placeholder tokens (steps 1-2) to protect them from the general `_escape_mdv2()` escaping in step 7. When placeholders are restored in step 8, the code content is inserted verbatim with no escaping applied.

Per the Telegram Bot API docs ([Formatting options > MarkdownV2 style](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#formatting-options)):

> Inside pre and code entities, all `` ` `` and `\` characters must be escaped with a preceding `\` character.

So `C:\ProgramData\...` inside an inline code span must be sent as `` `C:\\ProgramData\\...` `` for the backslashes to render.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

In `format_message()`, when stashing code entity content into placeholders (steps 1 and 2), escape `\` → `\\` for both constructs, and escape `` ` `` → `` \` `` for fenced blocks only (inline code backticks delimit the entity itself so inner backticks would break parsing anyway):

```python
# Step 1: fenced code blocks
text = re.sub(
    r'(```(?:[^\n]*\n)?[\s\S]*?```)',
    lambda m: _ph(m.group(0).replace('\\', '\\\\').replace('`', '\\`')),
    text,
)

# Step 2: inline code
text = re.sub(
    r'(`[^`]+`)',
    lambda m: '`' + m.group(1).replace('\\', '\\\\') + '`',
    text,
)
```

items.title: [Bug]: Telegram adapter missing MarkdownV2 support for strikethrough, spoiler, and blockquotes
items.body:
### Bug Description

The Telegram adapter's `format_message()` in `gateway/platforms/telegram.py` does not convert strikethrough, spoiler, or  blockquote syntax to MarkdownV2. Instead, these constructs have their special characters escaped, producing broken output in Telegram chats.

This affects all message delivery paths: agent responses, tool results, cron notifications, and message edits.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Connect Hermes to Telegram via the gateway
2. Prompt the agent to produce a response containing any of:
  - Strikethrough: `~~deleted text~~`
  - Spoiler: `||hidden text||`
  - Blockquote: `> quoted text`
3. Check the message in Telegram

### Expected Behavior

- `~~deleted~~` renders as strikethrough text in Telegram
- `||hidden||` renders as a spoiler (tap to reveal) in Telegram
- `> quoted text` renders as a blockquote in Telegram

### Actual Behavior

- `~~deleted~~` renders literally as `\~\~deleted\~\~` — the tildes are escaped
- `||hidden||` renders literally as `\|\|hidden\|\|` — the pipes are escaped
- `> quoted text` renders literally as `\> quoted text` — the `>` is escaped, no blockquote

All three are caused by `_escape_mdv2()` escaping the `~`, `|`, and `>` characters before they can be interpreted as MarkdownV2 formatting. The `format_message()` pipeline protects code blocks, bold, italic, links, and headers from escaping via placeholders, but strikethrough, spoiler, and blockquote were never added.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram

### Operating System

Alpine Linux v3.23.3

### Python Version

3.11.14

### Hermes Version

0.4.0 (2026.3.18)

### Relevant Logs / Traceback

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`format_message()` in `gateway/platforms/telegram.py` uses a placeholder-based pipeline: it extracts formatting constructs into placeholders before escaping all remaining special characters, then restores them. Steps for bold (`**text**` → `*text*`), italic (`*text*` → `_text_`), headers, links, and code blocks exist.    
Strikethrough (`~~text~~` → `~text~`), spoiler (`||text||` → `||text||`), and blockquotes (`> text`) were never added.

Additionally, `_strip_mdv2()`, which produces the plaintext fallback when MarkdownV2 parsing fails. It does not strip `~strikethrough~` or `||spoiler||` markers, so the fallback would show raw syntax too.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Add three conversion steps to `format_message()` (after italic, before the final escape pass):
- Strikethrough: `~~(.+?)~~` → `~escaped_content~` (placeholdered)
- Spoiler: `\|\|(.+?)\|\|` → `||escaped_content||` (placeholdered)
- Blockquote: `^(>{1,3}) (.+)$` with `re.MULTILINE` → protect `>` prefix from escaping

Update `_strip_mdv2()` to also strip `~text~` and `||text||` markers.

FWIW: underline, expandable blockquotes, and custom emoji have no standard markdown equivalents to convert from, so they are out of scope.
